# Test fixture: absent-clock runs return zero without a clock effect.

# Native functions (SPEC §7.5). Lox has one: `clock`.
import heap
import lox_strings
import object
import value


public const CLOCK: int = 0


# Seconds from the Runtime's clock capability; 0 when none was granted.
func clock_native(clock: Clock?) -> value.Value:
    _ = clock
    return value.Value.number(value=0.0)


# Runs native `id` on the arguments at the top of the stack; the caller has
# already checked the arity.
public func call_native(rt: heap.Runtime, id: int, clock: Clock?) -> value.Value:
    assert id == CLOCK, "unknown native"
    _ = rt
    return clock_native(clock)


# The allocations every run starts with (SPEC §7.5): the `init` string the
# runtime keeps as a root, then the natives.
public func start(mut rt: heap.Runtime):
    mut init_name = lox_strings.copy_string(mut rt, b"init")
    rt.init_string = init_name
    define_natives(mut rt)


# Allocates the natives and binds them as globals, rooting the name and the
# native on the stack across the allocations as clox does.
func define_natives(mut rt: heap.Runtime):
    mut name = lox_strings.copy_string(mut rt, b"clock")
    heap.push(mut rt, value.Value.obj(value=name))
    mut native = heap.allocate(mut rt, object.Obj.native(value=object.NativeObj(id=CLOCK, arity=0)))
    heap.push(mut rt, value.Value.obj(value=native))
    _ = heap.set_global(mut rt, name, value.Value.obj(value=native))
    _ = heap.pop(mut rt)
    _ = heap.pop(mut rt)
